messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: High paging and sustained KV cache evictions on prod-cluster-3 since 12:03 UTC. Affected model: redwood/gptq-13b-awq-int8 (route: /v1/generate). P95 latency spike +1000ms, error rate up 3%.
Ana (eng-runtime): I'm seeing this correlate with the awq-int8 kernel rollout at ~09:45 UTC. Kernel selection changed to prefer AWQ for this model which reduces compute but increases per-key KV size in our current serialization layout. Cache footprint jumped ~4x for some sequences.
Max (oncall): Confirmed paging pressure on nodes serving gpu-pool-b. Swap spikes and io_wait climbing. Are requests being continuously batched causing larger KV materialization?
Ana (eng-runtime): Yes — continuous batching + AWQ KV layout = larger per-request KV arrays. Since we do dynamic KV caching (prefix-based), the increased size meant we crossed the eviction threshold and started thrashing. Continuous batching then kept touching evicted keys -> paging loop.
Liam (sre): Logs excerpt (summarized):
```
node=prod-node-17 io_wait=72% page_ins=18432 kv_cache_evictions=8341 model=gptq-awq-13b
route=/v1/generate p95_latency_ms=1218
```
Sara (support): We already have 3 customer tickets reporting timeouts in the last 30m (customers A, C, D). No reports of corrupted outputs. SLA impact: increased tail latency and a few 504s.
Max (oncall): Immediate mitigations we can try (ordered):
1) Route heavy customers to fp16/gptq variant to reduce KV size. Quick config via routing API:
```
# set routing override to model_variant fp16 for customer-C
POST /internal/route/override
{ "customer_id": "C", "model": "redwood/gptq-13b", "variant": "fp16" }
```
2) Reduce continuous batch window and max tokens: lower continuous_batch_size and batch_timeout_ms to shrink in-flight KV.
```
# runtime config patch
PATCH /internal/runtime/config
{ "continuous_batch_max_tokens": 256, "continuous_batch_timeout_ms": 10 }
```
3) Apply kernel fallback flag for the model group to force non-AWQ kernel until we have a proper KV layout fix:
```
# temporary kernel override
PATCH /internal/models/redwood/gptq-13b/flags
{ "kernel_override": "fp16_fallback", "reason": "paging-hotfix" }
```
Ana (eng-runtime): I'm pushing the kernel_override now to gpu-pool-b. Rolling to 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 5 minutes. Also starting a scaling job to add 2 extra nodes to the pool to buy time.
ops-bot: deploy job started: rollout kernel_override -> rollout_id=r-5523 status=started
Liam (sre): Scaling action request accepted; adding 2 nodes (prod-node-30, prod-node-31). Expect provisioning in ~4m.
Ana (eng-runtime): Patch applied to 25% at 12:20, 100% at 12:27 UTC. Observed drop in page_ins and evictions within 90s. p95 back down to ~220ms.
Max (oncall): Good. Noting customer routing changes for C and D applied as well. Support, please acknowledge impacted customers and tell them we're mitigating, ETA ~20m.
Sara (support): Notified customers A,C,D with interim ETA. Will escalate any urgent ones.
Ana (eng-runtime): Quick post-mortem notes here: root cause = kernel selection heuristic favored AWQ int8 path without checking estimated KV footprint for continuous-batching workloads. The AWQ serialization uses a denser per-token representation that expands in memory when materialized into the runtime KV layout. We need a gating eval that measures KV bytes per token across representative prompts before switching kernels.
Max (oncall): Handoff: I'm taking the incident for the next 3 hours. Ana, please stay reachable for follow-up. Liam will track infra autoscale costs and any residual IO. Ops-bot, keep an eye on page_ins metric and fire if >2000 for 15m.
ops-bot: alert rule updated: metric=kv_page_ins threshold=2000 window=15m -> notify=#incidents, @oncall
Ana (eng-runtime): Follow-ups/tasks:
- Create regression test with continuous batching + representative long prompts to measure KV size for each quant path. (owner: Ana)
- Add kernel-selection gating rule into model onboarding pipeline. (owner: Research/Applied ML)
- Update runtime to expose per-request KV_bytes metric to make future incidents quicker. (owner: eng-runtime)
- Postmortem and customer-impact summary. (owner: Max)
Max (oncall): I'll file the postmortem template now and tag the SRE/ML teams. Closing note: no data loss, no credentials exposed. Primary impact: increased latency and 504s for a subset of traffic. We'll schedule a follow-up review tomorrow morning 09:30 UTC.
Ana (eng-runtime): Thanks team. Leaving the kernel_override flag in place for 24h while we add KV-size checks. If anyone sees re-occurrence, @Max (oncall) is primary.
Max (oncall): Acknowledged. Switching to incident-followup channel for detailed timeline and next steps. :white_check_mark:"
